claims.text: Amazon reported AWS sales up 37% to $42.2 billion and AWS operating income of $16.6 billion, versus $10.2 billion a year earlier.
The issuer says its $62.6 billion of quarterly net income includes $53.4 billion of nonoperating pretax other income, primarily from Anthropic investments. That amount is not operating profit.
claims.source_cue: non-operating pre-tax other income of $53.4 billion

claims.text: Amazon guided third-quarter 2026 net sales to $197–202 billion, or 9–12% year-on-year growth, with roughly 80 basis points of currency headwind. The issuer says growth excluding Prime Day's timing effect in both years would be nearly 400 basis points higher.

reads.question: How much of the earnings change reflects recurring operations, given the issuer-described nonoperating investment gain?

claims.text: Lilly attributed 48% year-on-year revenue growth to 60% higher volume, partly offset by a 13% decline in realized prices. Its issuer-defined Key Products basket reached $15.7 billion, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound.
claims.source_cue: driven by a 60% increase in volume

claims.text: Lilly says a $2.78 midpoint rise in underlying non-GAAP EPS guidance was more than offset by $3.03 of acquired in-process R&D charges, leaving updated full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance at $35.50–36.50. These are issuer-defined non-GAAP measures.
Lilly raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $82–85 billion to $85–87 billion. This is issuer guidance, not a realized result.

reads.question: Will the issuer's reported volume gains continue to outweigh lower realized pricing?

claims.text: Home Depot reported total sales up 5.7%, while comparable sales rose 1.7% and U.S. comparable sales rose 1.3%. The different growth rates should not be treated as the same measure.
claims.source_cue: Comparable sales for the second quarter

claims.text: The company reaffirmed fiscal-2026 guidance for roughly 2.5–4.5% total sales growth and flat-to-2% comparable sales growth. Its guidance assumes IEEPA tariff refunds partly offset higher input costs.

reads.question: What explains the gap between total-sales growth and comparable-sales growth, and is that mix durable?

claims.text: JPMorgan says net interest income excluding Markets rose 4% to $23.7 billion, with higher deposit, card and wholesale-loan balances largely offset by lower rates. Markets revenue rose 35% to $12.1 billion; these are issuer-defined business lenses, not the 10-Q's reported net revenue.

Reported net income rose 41% to $21.2 billion, but the issuer says it rose 13% excluding significant items, to $16.9 billion. The quarter included a $4.6 billion Visa-share gain and $1.0 billion of other investment gains; the excluding-items result is non-GAAP.

Credit costs were $2.5 billion, including $2.4 billion of net charge-offs and a $149 million reserve build, primarily in Wholesale. These are quarterly firmwide credit-cost measures, not a forecast of future losses.

reads.question: How much of the earnings gain persists without the investment gains, and do credit costs change as loan balances grow?

claims.text: ExxonMobil says Energy Products earnings improved from the prior quarter on stronger U.S. Gulf Coast utilization and record diesel production, partly offset by scheduled maintenance. This is segment commentary, not a consolidated earnings bridge.

The issuer says record Permian production above 1.8 million oil-equivalent barrels per day and no Kazakhstan disruption helped Upstream earnings sequentially, while Middle East disruptions partly offset those benefits. Production is not revenue or profit.
claims.source_cue: partly offset by the Middle East disruptions

claims.text: ExxonMobil planned a fourth-quarter 2026 startup for its fifth Guyana FPSO, adding 250 thousand barrels per day of capacity. That is a project plan and capacity figure, not realized production or earnings.

reads.question: Will production reliability offset disruption and maintenance costs, and will the planned Guyana capacity start in fourth-quarter 2026?

claims.text: Caterpillar says second-quarter sales and revenues rose 24% to $20.543 billion, mainly on $3.1 billion of higher volume and $595 million of favorable price realization. Higher equipment sales to end users drove much of the volume gain.
claims.source_cue: higher sales of equipment to end users

claims.text: The issuer says second-quarter operating profit of $4.295 billion included $392 million of expected IEEPA tariff recoveries. The recovery is in reported operating profit, but this exhibit does not establish how much would recur.

reads.question: Will end-user equipment sales sustain the volume gain without the same tariff recovery in a later quarter?
